name: Calibration Workflow Redesign
description: Redesigned the sensor calibration workflow for EMG research software.
longDesc: During my time at Delsys, I redesigned the EMG calibration workflow, a critical step that allows researchers to normalize sensors to participants’ muscles for accurate study results. I overhauled the UX, UI, and user flows, introducing multi-sensor calibration to save researchers time while increasing consistency and reliability in their data collection. This project was completed in collaboration with a team of three, highlighting both coordination and design problem-solving in a fast-paced environment.

name: Echo
description: Analyzes user reviews for places with sentiment analysis.
longDesc: A React web app that displays insights on user reviews of a searched query. These insights include graphs with breakdowns of positive, negative, neutral reviews, sentiment over time, and an AI-generated summary of most recent reviews. The app helps users quickly understand public opinion about different places without sifting through hundreds of reviews. All information fetched from an external API.

caseStudy.problem: Users had to sift through hundreds of online reviews to get a sense of public opinion.
caseStudy.goal: Create a tool to surface review trends and sentiment in a digestible visual format.
caseStudy.approach: I designed several UI iterations in Figma focusing on clarity and visual hierarchy. Key metrics like overview, sentiment breakdown and images were prioritized.

designIterations.title: Low-Fidelity Mock
designIterations.notes: Created a basic layout framework with placeholder elements to establish general page structure. Visual styling was minimal, with no defined hierarchy or content yet. Feedback focused on maintaining clean separation between blocks to avoid clutter.

designIterations.title: Mid-Fidelity Mock
designIterations.notes: Introduced content and visual hierarchy through grouped sections, light gray backgrounds, and clear labels. This version helped validate layout logic and user flows.

designIterations.title: Final Design
designIterations.notes: Final iteration applied a polished visual style and color scheme, enhancing clarity and engagement. The organization of each section was very strategic, prioritizing high level information first and more specific details later. Each section was differentiated with dark backgrounds, accent colors, and refined typography. Interactive elements and data visualizations were styled for readability. This version addressed clutter concerns and clearly guided the user's eye across the content.

outcomes: Improved user understanding of sentiment breakdown at a glance
Positive feedback on design clarity and speed of insights
First project to integrate D3.js charts

name: strategy.town
description: A project in which I extended current functionality with new user stories.
longDesc: The project extended existing single-player functionality to support real-time multiplayer interactions, user progress tracking, and personalized statistics dashboards. Players can track wins, streaks, and scores over time, adding a competitive and engaging layer to the games. The project demonstrates both front-end development skills and system design thinking required to manage multiplayer game state and user data.

name: Travel Journal
description: Travel journal of my trips while studying abroad.
longDesc: This was my first solo React project, and a great way to compile my favorite memories and images from when I was studying abroad.

name: Recipe Finder
description: Discover and organize recipes tailored to your preferences and dietary needs
longDesc: The app allows users to discover a wide variety of recipes tailored to their dietary preferences and needs. Users can save their favorite recipes and even create shopping lists based on selected ingredients. The app also offers features like user authentication, allowing for a secure and personalized cooking experience that evolves with the user's tastes and preferences.

caseStudy.problem: Users struggle to find recipes that match their dietary preferences and often forget ingredients they need to buy.
caseStudy.goal: Create an app that allows users to discover recipes, save favorites, and create shopping lists.
caseStudy.approach: I developed a mobile app using Android Studio and Java, integrating Firebase for user authentication and data storage. The app features a RESTful API to fetch recipes based on user preferences.
outcomes: Created a fully functional mobile app with user authentication
Implemented features for saving favorite recipes and creating shopping lists
Demonstrated ability to integrate Firebase and RESTful APIs in mobile development
